growth_experiences: Early in his career he had severe stage fright, but through extensive practice and seeking feedback from more senior comedians, he gradually improved his stage control and built fairly stable confidence; this is his early experience of facing difficulties and successfully improving.

special_situations.event: Poor self-evaluation after the last performance at the local theater
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not famous yet, it means I have no talent and am doomed not to succeed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Takes 'becoming famous as soon as possible' as the sole criterion of success or failure, denying any gradual progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I had talent, I would be famous by now; I will not succeed

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others succeed, it means I fail or lack the key abilities they have
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly compares himself with successful people to evaluate his self-worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They have things I do not have; I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: Negative predictions arise at every performance or when seeing successful comedians
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If every performance does not immediately receive widespread recognition, it means I can never succeed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Presets failure in advance to reduce disappointment, and avoids discussing self-doubt with friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never make it big

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback from audiences or peers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If praise does not come from an authority or is not specific enough, it is not credible and does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Denies or dismisses positive evaluations, attributing them to 'politeness'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; they do not really recognize me
